qe: After decreasing by 25%, the cost of a jacket becomes ₹4,500. Find its original cost.
qh: 25% की कमी के बाद, एक जैकेट का मूल्य ₹4,500 हो जाता है। इसका मूल मूल्य ज्ञात कीजिए।
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
$25\% = \frac{1}{4}$.
Original Cost : Decreased Cost $= 4 : (4 - 1) = 4 : 3$.
Given: 3 units $= ₹4500 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = \frac{4500}{3} = ₹1500$.
Original Cost = 4 units $= 4 \times 1500 = ₹6000$.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Original cost ko $100\%$ maan lo.
$25\%$ decrease ke baad cost $= 100\% - 25\% = 75\%$.
Given: $75\% = ₹4500$.
$1\% = \frac{4500}{75} = ₹60$.
Original Cost ($100\%$) $= 60 \times 100 = ₹6000$.

qe: The price of a laptop was ₹80,000 last year. This year, its price decreased by 20%. What is the price (in ₹) of the laptop this year?
qh: पिछले वर्ष एक लैपटॉप का मूल्य ₹80,000 था। इस वर्ष इसके मूल्य में 20% की कमी आई। इस वर्ष लैपटॉप का मूल्य (₹ में) क्या है?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
$20\% = \frac{1}{5}$.
Original Price : New Price $= 5 : 4$.
Given: 5 units $= ₹80000 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = \frac{80000}{5} = ₹16000$.
New Price = 4 units $= 4 \times 16000 = ₹64000$.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Original Price $= 100\% = ₹80000$.
Price $20\%$ decrease hone ke baad bacha $= 80\%$.
New Price $= 80\% \text{ of } 80000 = \frac{80}{100} \times 80000 = ₹64000$.

qe: Rahul's salary in 2021 was ₹30,000. He gets an increment of 10% every year. What was his salary in 2023?
qh: 2021 में राहुल का वेतन ₹30,000 था। उसे प्रत्येक वर्ष 10% की वेतन वृद्धि मिलती है। 2023 में उसका वेतन क्या था?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
$10\% = \frac{1}{10}$.
Har saal salary ka ratio $= 10 : 11$.
2 saal (2021 se 2023) me ratio $= 10^2 : 11^2 = 100 : 121$.
Given: 100 units $= ₹30000 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = ₹300$.
Salary in 2023 = 121 units $= 121 \times 300 = ₹36300$.

Method 2 (100-Base / Successive Formula):
Two successive hikes of $10\%$:
Net hike $= 10 + 10 + \frac{10 \times 10}{100} = 21\%$.
Salary in 2023 $= 30000 + (21\% \text{ of } 30000) = 30000 + 6300 = ₹36300$.

qe: A motorcycle is sold for ₹72,000, which is 20% less than its original price. What was the original price of the motorcycle?
qh: एक मोटरसाइकिल ₹72,000 में बेची जाती है, जो इसके मूल मूल्य से 20% कम है। मोटरसाइकिल का मूल मूल्य क्या था?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
$20\% = \frac{1}{5}$.
Original Price : Selling Price $= 5 : 4$.
Given: 4 units $= ₹72000 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = \frac{72000}{4} = ₹18000$.
Original Price = 5 units $= 5 \times 18000 = ₹90000$.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Original price $= 100\%$.
Selling price after $20\%$ reduction $= 80\%$.
Given: $80\% = ₹72000$.
$1\% = \frac{72000}{80} = ₹900$.
Original Price ($100\%$) $= 900 \times 100 = ₹90000$.

qe: If 25% of 40% of a number is 180, then 15% of that number is:
qh: यदि किसी संख्या के 40% का 25% मान 180 है, तो उस संख्या का 15% क्या होगा?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
$25\% = \frac{1}{4}$ aur $40\% = \frac{2}{5}$.
Fractional part $= \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{1}{10}$.
Given: $\frac{1}{10}$ of number $= 180 \implies \text{Number} = 1800$.
Ab number ka $15\%$ nikaalna hai:
$15\% = \frac{3}{20} \implies \frac{3}{20} \times 1800 = 3 \times 90 = 270$.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Let the number be $100\%$.
$40\% \text{ of } 100\% = 40\%$.
$25\% \text{ of } 40\% = 10\%$.
Given: $10\% = 180$.
$1\% = 18$.
Required $15\% = 15 \times 18 = 270$.

qe: During the first year, the population of a town increased by 10% and during the second year it decreased by 10%. At the end of the second year, its population was 59,400. What was the population at the beginning of the first year?
qh: पहले वर्ष के दौरान एक कस्बे की जनसंख्या में 10% की वृद्धि हुई और दूसरे वर्ष के दौरान इसमें 10% की कमी आई। दूसरे वर्ष के अंत में इसकी जनसंख्या 59,400 थी। पहले वर्ष की शुरुआत में जनसंख्या कितनी थी?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Year 1 (+10%): $10 : 11$.
Year 2 (-10%): $10 : 9$.
Initial Population : Final Population $= (10 \times 10) : (11 \times 9) = 100 : 99$.
Given: 99 units $= 59400 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = \frac{59400}{99} = 600$.
Initial Population = 100 units $= 100 \times 600 = 60000$.

Method 2 (Successive Formula):
Net percentage change $= +10 - 10 - \frac{10 \times 10}{100} = -1\%$.
Final population $= 100\% - 1\% = 99\%$.
$99\% = 59400 \implies 1\% = 600$.
Initial population ($100\%$) $= 600 \times 100 = 60000$.

qe: Pankaj gets a 10% increase in his sales in the first year and a 20% increase in the second year. If his present sales amount is ₹1,58,400, what was his sales amount two years ago?
qh: पंकज की बिक्री में पहले वर्ष 10% और दूसरे वर्ष 20% की वृद्धि होती है। यदि उसकी वर्तमान बिक्री राशि ₹1,58,400 है, तो दो वर्ष पहले उसकी बिक्री राशि क्या थी?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Year 1 (+10%): $10\% = \frac{1}{10} \implies 10 : 11$.
Year 2 (+20%): $20\% = \frac{1}{5} \implies 5 : 6$.
Initial Sales : Present Sales $= (10 \times 5) : (11 \times 6) = 50 : 66 = 25 : 33$.
Given: 33 units $= ₹158400 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = \frac{158400}{33} = ₹4800$.
Initial Sales = 25 units $= 25 \times 4800 = ₹120000$.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Net increase $= 10 + 20 + \frac{10 \times 20}{100} = 32\%$.
Present Sales $= 100\% + 32\% = 132\%$.
Given: $132\% = ₹158400$.
$1\% = \frac{158400}{132} = ₹1200$.
Sales 2 years ago ($100\%$) $= 1200 \times 100 = ₹120000$.

qe: After a discount of 15%, an electronic gadget is available for ₹1,19,000. Find its marked price.
qh: 15% की छूट के बाद, एक इलेक्ट्रॉनिक उपकरण ₹1,19,000 में उपलब्ध है। इसका अंकित मूल्य ज्ञात कीजिए।
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
$15\% = \frac{3}{20}$.
Marked Price : Discounted Price $= 20 : (20 - 3) = 20 : 17$.
Given: 17 units $= ₹119000 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = \frac{119000}{17} = ₹7000$.
Marked Price = 20 units $= 20 \times 7000 = ₹140000$.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Marked Price $= 100\%$.
Price after $15\%$ discount $= 85\%$.
Given: $85\% = ₹119000$.
$1\% = \frac{119000}{85} = ₹1400$.
Marked Price ($100\%$) $= 1400 \times 100 = ₹140000$.

qe: Two years ago, the population of a town was 80,000. Due to industrial development, it increases every year at the rate of 5%. The present population of the town is:
qh: दो वर्ष पहले, एक शहर की जनसंख्या 80,000 थी। औद्योगिक विकास के कारण, इसमें प्रत्येक वर्ष 5% की दर से वृद्धि होती है। शहर की वर्तमान जनसंख्या क्या है?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
$5\% = \frac{1}{20}$.
Har saal population ratio $= 20 : 21$.
2 saal me compound change $= 20^2 : 21^2 = 400 : 441$.
Given: 400 units $= 80000 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = \frac{80000}{400} = 200$.
Present population = 441 units $= 441 \times 200 = 88200$.

Method 2 (100-Base / Successive Formula):
2 saal ka net percentage increase $= 5 + 5 + \frac{5 \times 5}{100} = 10.25\%$.
Present population $= 80000 + (10.25\% \text{ of } 80000) = 80000 + 8200 = 88200$.

qe: Sumit gets a 5% increase in his sale amount in the first year and 10% in the second year. If his present sale is ₹1,38,600, what was his sale (in ₹) two years ago?
qh: सुमित की बिक्री राशि में पहले वर्ष 5% और दूसरे वर्ष 10% की वृद्धि होती है। यदि उसकी वर्तमान बिक्री ₹1,38,600 है, तो दो वर्ष पहले उसकी बिक्री (₹ में) क्या थी?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Year 1 (+5%): $5\% = \frac{1}{20} \implies 20 : 21$.
Year 2 (+10%): $10\% = \frac{1}{10} \implies 10 : 11$.
Initial Sale : Present Sale $= (20 \times 10) : (21 \times 11) = 200 : 231$.
Given: 231 units $= ₹138600 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = \frac{138600}{231} = ₹600$.
Sale 2 years ago = 200 units $= 200 \times 600 = ₹120000$.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Net increase over 2 years $= 5 + 10 + \frac{5 \times 10}{100} = 15.5\%$.
Present sale $= 100\% + 15.5\% = 115.5\%$.
Given: $115.5\% = ₹138600$.
$1\% = \frac{138600}{115.5} = ₹1200$.
Original sale ($100\%$) $= 1200 \times 100 = ₹120000$.

qe: The price of an article is increased by k%. The new price was decreased by k% later. Now the latest price is ₹P. What was the original price of the article?
qh: एक वस्तु के मूल्य में k% की वृद्धि की जाती है। बाद में नए मूल्य में k% की कमी की जाती है। अब नवीनतम मूल्य ₹P है। वस्तु का मूल मूल्य क्या था?
e:
Method 1 (Successive Multiplier Method):
Pehle $k\%$ badhane par factor $= \left(1 + \frac{k}{100}\right)$.
Fir $k\%$ ghatane par factor $= \left(1 - \frac{k}{100}\right)$.
Net Multiplier $= \left(1 + \frac{k}{100}\right)\left(1 - \frac{k}{100}\right) = 1 - \frac{k^2}{10000} = \frac{10000 - k^2}{10000}$.
Latest Price $= \text{Original Price} \times \frac{10000 - k^2}{10000} = P$.
$\implies \text{Original Price} = \frac{10000 P}{10000 - k^2}$.

Method 2 (100-Base / Direct Loss Formula):
Jab kisi value ko pehle $k\%$ badhayein aur fir $k\%$ ghatayein, toh net loss $= \frac{k^2}{100}\%$ hota hai.
Final percentage $= 100\% - \frac{k^2}{100}\% = \frac{10000 - k^2}{100}\%$.
Ye value $P$ ke barabar hai:
$\frac{10000 - k^2}{10000} \times \text{Original} = P \implies \text{Original} = \frac{10000 P}{10000 - k^2}$.

qe: The population of a village was 2,50,000. It increased by 10% in the first year and increased by 20% in the second year. Its population after two years is:
qh: एक गाँव की जनसंख्या 2,50,000 थी। पहले वर्ष में इसमें 10% की वृद्धि हुई और दूसरे वर्ष में 20% की वृद्धि हुई। दो वर्ष बाद इसकी जनसंख्या क्या होगी?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Year 1 (+10%): $10 : 11$.
Year 2 (+20%): $5 : 6$.
Initial Population : Final Population $= (10 \times 5) : (11 \times 6) = 50 : 66 = 25 : 33$.
Given: 25 units $= 250000 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = 10000$.
Population after 2 years = 33 units $= 33 \times 10000 = 330000$.

Method 2 (100-Base / Successive Formula):
Two successive increases of $10\%$ and $20\%$:
Net increase $= 10 + 20 + \frac{10 \times 20}{100} = 32\%$.
Population after 2 years $= 250000 + (32\% \text{ of } 250000) = 250000 + 80000 = 330000$.

qe: The population of a town increases by 10% in the first year, decreases by 20% in the second year, and again increases by 30% in the third year. If the population at the beginning was 50,000, what will it be after 3 years?
qh: एक शहर की जनसंख्या पहले वर्ष में 10% बढ़ती है, दूसरे वर्ष में 20% घटती है, और तीसरे वर्ष में पुनः 30% बढ़ती है। यदि शुरुआत में जनसंख्या 50,000 थी, तो 3 वर्ष बाद यह कितनी होगी?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Year 1 (+10%): $10 : 11$.
Year 2 (-20%): $5 : 4$.
Year 3 (+30%): $10 : 13$.
Initial : Final $= (10 \times 5 \times 10) : (11 \times 4 \times 13) = 500 : 572$.
Given: 500 units $= 50000 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = 100$.
Population after 3 years = 572 units $= 572 \times 100 = 57200$.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Initial population $= 100$.
After Year 1 (+10%): $100 + 10 = 110$.
After Year 2 (-20%): $110 - (20\% \text{ of } 110) = 110 - 22 = 88$.
After Year 3 (+30%): $88 + (30\% \text{ of } 88) = 88 + 26.4 = 114.4$.
Population after 3 years $= 50000 \times \frac{114.4}{100} = 500 \times 114.4 = 57200$.

qe: The population of a city is 60,000. It increases by 10% in the first year and decreases by 5% in the second year. What will be the population of the city after 2 years?
qh: एक शहर की जनसंख्या 60,000 है। पहले वर्ष में इसमें 10% की वृद्धि होती है और दूसरे वर्ष में 5% की कमी होती है। 2 वर्ष बाद शहर की जनसंख्या क्या होगी?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Year 1 (+10%): $10\% = \frac{1}{10} \implies 10 : 11$.
Year 2 (-5%): $5\% = \frac{1}{20} \implies 20 : 19$.
Initial : Final $= (10 \times 20) : (11 \times 19) = 200 : 209$.
Given: 200 units $= 60000 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = \frac{60000}{200} = 300$.
Population after 2 years = 209 units $= 209 \times 300 = 62700$.

Method 2 (Successive Formula):
Net percentage change $= +10 - 5 + \frac{10 \times (-5)}{100} = 5 - 0.5 = +4.5\%$.
Population after 2 years $= 60000 + (4.5\% \text{ of } 60000) = 60000 + 2700 = 62700$.

qe: The price of a digital camera is first reduced by 20% and then increased by 40%. If the resulting price of the digital camera is ₹8,960, then what was its original price (in ₹)?
qh: एक डिजिटल कैमरे के मूल्य में पहले 20% की कमी की जाती है और फिर 40% की वृद्धि की जाती है। यदि डिजिटल कैमरे का परिणामी मूल्य ₹8,960 है, तो इसका मूल मूल्य (₹ में) क्या था?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Reduction: $20\% = \frac{1}{5} \implies 5 : 4$.
Increase: $40\% = \frac{2}{5} \implies 5 : 7$.
Initial Price : Resulting Price $= (5 \times 5) : (4 \times 7) = 25 : 28$.
Given: 28 units $= ₹8960 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = \frac{8960}{28} = ₹320$.
Original Price = 25 units $= 25 \times 320 = ₹8000$.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Initial Price $= 100\%$.
Net Change $= -20 + 40 + \frac{(-20) \times 40}{100} = 20 - 8 = +12\%$.
Resulting Price $= 100\% + 12\% = 112\%$.
Given: $112\% = ₹8960$.
$1\% = \frac{8960}{112} = ₹80$.
Original Price ($100\%$) $= 80 \times 100 = ₹8000$.

qe: The price of an electronic printer decreased by 10%, 10%, and 20% during the first three years. What will be the price of the printer after three years if the value at the beginning was ₹15,000?
qh: एक इलेक्ट्रॉनिक प्रिंटर के मूल्य में पहले तीन वर्षों के दौरान क्रमशः 10%, 10% और 20% की कमी आई। यदि शुरुआत में इसका मूल्य ₹15,000 था, तो तीन वर्ष बाद प्रिंटर का मूल्य क्या होगा?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Year 1 (-10%): $10 : 9$
Year 2 (-10%): $10 : 9$
Year 3 (-20%): $5 : 4$
Initial Value : Value after 3 years $= (10 \times 10 \times 5) : (9 \times 9 \times 4) = 500 : 324$.
Given: 500 units $= ₹15000 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = \frac{15000}{500} = ₹30$.
Price after 3 years = 324 units $= 324 \times 30 = ₹9720$.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Initial Value $= ₹15000$.
After Year 1: $15000 \times 0.90 = 13500$.
After Year 2: $13500 \times 0.90 = 12150$.
After Year 3: $12150 \times 0.80 = ₹9720$.

qe: The population of a town is 20,000. If the population increases by 10% in the first year, by 20% in the second year, and due to migration it decreases by 5% in the third year, what will be its population after 3 years?
qh: एक शहर की जनसंख्या 20,000 है। यदि पहले वर्ष में जनसंख्या में 10% की वृद्धि होती है, दूसरे वर्ष में 20% की वृद्धि होती है, और प्रवास के कारण तीसरे वर्ष में 5% की कमी होती है, तो 3 वर्ष बाद इसकी जनसंख्या क्या होगी?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Year 1 (+10%): $10 : 11$
Year 2 (+20%): $5 : 6$
Year 3 (-5%): $20 : 19$
Initial : Final $= (10 \times 5 \times 20) : (11 \times 6 \times 19) = 1000 : 1254$.
Given: 1000 units $= 20000 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = 20$.
Population after 3 years = 1254 units $= 1254 \times 20 = 25080$.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Initial population $= 20000$.
After Year 1 (+10%): $20000 + 2000 = 22000$.
After Year 2 (+20%): $22000 + 4400 = 26400$.
After Year 3 (-5%): $26400 - (5\% \text{ of } 26400) = 26400 - 1320 = 25080$.

qe: Deepak studies the pattern of daily sale of a grocery shop. He finds that on Monday, the sale was decreased by 20% in comparison to the sale on Sunday. On Tuesday, the sale was increased by 20% in comparison to the sale of Monday. If the sale on Tuesday was of ₹2,880, how much was the sale on Sunday?
qh: दीपक एक किराना दुकान की दैनिक बिक्री के पैटर्न का अध्ययन करता है। वह पाता है कि रविवार की बिक्री की तुलना में सोमवार को बिक्री में 20% की कमी आई। सोमवार की बिक्री की तुलना में मंगलवार को बिक्री में 20% की वृद्धि हुई। यदि मंगलवार को ₹2,880 की बिक्री हुई, तो रविवार को बिक्री कितनी थी?
e:
Method 1 (Equal Change Direct Shortcut):
Jab kisi base value ko pehle $x\%$ ghatayein aur fir $x\%$ badhayein, toh net loss $= \frac{x^2}{100}\%$ hota hai.
Net loss $= \frac{20^2}{100}\% = 4\%$.
Sunday ki sale ke mukable Tuesday ki sale $= 100\% - 4\% = 96\%$.
Given: $96\% = ₹2880$.
$1\% = \frac{2880}{96} = ₹30$.
Sunday ki sale ($100\%$) $= 30 \times 100 = ₹3000$.

Method 2 (Ratio Method):
Monday (-20%): $5 : 4$.
Tuesday (+20%): $5 : 6$.
Sunday : Tuesday $= (5 \times 5) : (4 \times 6) = 25 : 24$.
Given: 24 units $= ₹2880 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = \frac{2880}{24} = ₹120$.
Sunday's sale = 25 units $= 25 \times 120 = ₹3000$.

qe: The price of a car increases by 25% in the first year and decreases by 20% in the second year. If its final price becomes ₹4,80,000, find the original price of the car.
qh: एक कार के मूल्य में पहले वर्ष 25% की वृद्धि होती है और दूसरे वर्ष 20% की कमी होती है। यदि इसका अंतिम मूल्य ₹4,80,000 हो जाता है, तो कार का मूल मूल्य ज्ञात कीजिए।
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Year 1 (+25%): $25\% = \frac{1}{4} \implies 4 : 5$.
Year 2 (-20%): $20\% = \frac{1}{5} \implies 5 : 4$.
Original Price : Final Price $= (4 \times 5) : (5 \times 4) = 20 : 20 = 1 : 1$.
Since ratio is $1 : 1$, Original Price $=$ Final Price $= ₹480000$.

Method 2 (Successive Formula):
Net Change $= +25 - 20 + \frac{25 \times (-20)}{100} = 5 - 5 = 0\%$.
Kyunki net change $0\%$ hai, isliye price unaltered rahega.
Original Price $= ₹480000$.

qe: 10% of the inhabitants of a village having died of an epidemic, a panic set in, during which 20% of the remaining inhabitants left the village. The population was then reduced to 14,400. What was the number of inhabitants initially?
qh: एक महामारी से एक गाँव के 10% निवासियों की मृत्यु हो जाने के बाद, दहशत फैल गई, जिसके दौरान शेष निवासियों में से 20% ने गाँव छोड़ दिया। इसके बाद जनसंख्या घटकर 14,400 हो गई। शुरुआत में निवासियों की संख्या क्या थी?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Step 1 (-10%): $10 : 9$.
Step 2 (-20%): $5 : 4$.
Initial Population : Final Population $= (10 \times 5) : (9 \times 4) = 50 : 36 = 25 : 18$.
Given: 18 units $= 14400 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = \frac{14400}{18} = 800$.
Initial Population = 25 units $= 25 \times 800 = 20000$.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Initial population $= 100\%$.
After epidemic deaths: $100 - 10 = 90\%$.
After migration of remaining: $90\% - (20\% \text{ of } 90\%) = 90 - 18 = 72\%$.
Given: $72\% = 14400$.
$1\% = \frac{14400}{72} = 200$.
Initial Population ($100\%$) $= 200 \times 100 = 20000$.

qe: On account of a viral outbreak, 10% of the population of a village died. Out of the remaining population, 25% fled due to panic. If the present population is 5,400, then what was the population of the village before the outbreak?
qh: वायरस के प्रकोप के कारण एक गाँव की 10% जनसंख्या की मृत्यु हो गई। शेष जनसंख्या में से 25% दहशत के कारण भाग गए। यदि वर्तमान जनसंख्या 5,400 है, तो प्रकोप से पहले गाँव की जनसंख्या क्या थी?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Step 1 (-10%): $10 : 9$.
Step 2 (-25%): $4 : 3$.
Initial Population : Present Population $= (10 \times 4) : (9 \times 3) = 40 : 27$.
Given: 27 units $= 5400 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = \frac{5400}{27} = 200$.
Initial Population = 40 units $= 40 \times 200 = 8000$.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Initial population $= 100\%$.
After deaths: $100 - 10 = 90\%$.
After panic exit: $90\% - (25\% \text{ of } 90\%) = 90 - 22.5 = 67.5\%$.
Given: $67.5\% = 5400$.
$1\% = \frac{5400}{67.5} = 80$.
Initial Population ($100\%$) $= 80 \times 100 = 8000$.
